title: Audit log batching tier changes in inference config (who/when/what changed)
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Audit logs now record changes to batching tier selection in config (actor, timestamp, old/new values, scope). No API surface changes; adds audit event types for enterprise change management.
body:
Summary: This PR adds explicit audit log entries when the batching tier in inference configuration changes (fast / standard / cost_efficient). The goal is to support enterprise change management and customer support workflows by capturing who changed the tier, when it was changed, and what changed (old value -> new value), including the scope of the config (org/project/deployment/route/model if applicable).

Motivation / context: We are rolling out workload-aware batching defaults and exposing a tier selector in Console/API. During beta we saw customer confusion around tier vs explicit overrides (SUP-18510) and internal requests for a standard troubleshooting playbook (INT-3301). For enterprise customers, we also need auditable change trails for performance-affecting config (tier changes can alter queue delay, batch formation, and latency characteristics).

What’s included: 1) New audit event types and schema: - event_type: inference.config.update - event_subtype: batching.tier.change - target_resource_type: inference_config - target_resource_id: (deployment_id or route_config_id, depending on surface) - fields captured: actor_id, actor_type (user/service), actor_email (if user), org_id, project_id, request_id, source (console|api|config_import|helm), old_value, new_value, scope (route, model, region labels where available). 2) Server-side detection of tier changes: - We compute a minimal diff for the config update request and emit a dedicated audit entry only when batching_tier changes. - We intentionally do NOT emit an audit record on requests that only change explicit batching knobs (max_batch_size, max_queue_delay_ms, etc.) in this PR. Those changes are already captured by the existing generic config update audit record, but they were too noisy to be useful as a signal in enterprise review workflows. (Follow-up proposed: add targeted audit subtypes for a small set of high-risk knobs.) 3) Redaction / safety: - Audit payloads exclude prompt contents and any request bodies unrelated to config changes. - We do not log bearer tokens; only request_id and authenticated principal identifiers. - IP address and user-agent are recorded only for user actors; service-to-service actors record only service name.

Behavior details / edge cases: - Explicit config vs tier defaults: The audit entry is emitted on changes to the configured tier selector field (batching_tier), not when the effective tier changes due to backend defaulting. This keeps audit trails attributable to an actor action rather than server behavior. - “Unset” behavior: If a customer removes batching_tier (null) and falls back to server default, we emit old_value=<previous tier>, new_value="(unset)", and include default_resolution="server_default" in the metadata string. - Config import/export: For config_import (including Private helm/installer pipelines), we use the authenticated service principal as the actor and set source=config_import or source=helm based on the request origin header.

Example audit entry (redacted): {"timestamp":"2025-03-20T18:41:09.442Z","event_type":"inference.config.update","event_subtype":"batching.tier.change","org_id":"org_7n3...","project_id":"proj_2a9...","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"user_91f...","actor_email":"alice@customer.com","source":"console","request_id":"req_01HT...","target_resource_type":"inference_config","target_resource_id":"routecfg_4d2...","message":"Batching tier changed","diff":"batching_tier: standard -> cost_efficient","scope":"route=/v1/chat.completions model=rw-open-llama-70b region=us-east-1"}

Implementation notes: - Control plane: Added a dedicated diff detector for batching_tier in the config update path. The logic sits after validation (so we don’t audit failed updates) and before persistence (so we can include request_id + actor fields consistently). - Audit pipeline: Reuses existing audit sink (same path as RBAC policy and key management changes). Added a new subtype constant and wired to the audit event formatter.

Files / areas changed (high level): - control-plane/config: compute_config_diff + emit_audit_events - audit/events: new subtype constant + formatting - console/backend: propagate source header for config updates - private/control-plane: ensure helm/config_import sets source correctly - tests: unit tests for tier diff detection; integration test asserting audit emission on tier change

Test plan: - Unit: audit diff computation: tier change, unset, no-op, invalid enum rejected (no audit) - Integration: config update API emits audit event only on tier changes; verifies actor attribution and diff string - Manual: via staging Console: change tier on a route config and confirm audit event appears in audit viewer and is exportable

Rollout: - Safe to deploy behind existing audit pipeline. No feature flag required. - For Private deployments, events appear in the same audit sink; no schema migrations needed (subtype is a new string).

Checklist: - [x] Added/updated tests - [x] Verified no sensitive payloads logged - [x] Documented new audit subtype in internal audit taxonomy - [x] Confirmed with SRE that event volume is bounded (tier changes are low frequency)

Review conversation (condensed):

Allison Grant (requested changes): Can we ensure we don’t log request bodies / config blobs for these events? Also please confirm this won’t spam audit logs on periodic reconciles.

Ethan Park (author): Confirmed: audit entry is emitted only when batching_tier differs between persisted config and the validated update payload; no entries on reconcile loops. Payload stores only the old/new scalar tier values and a short scope string; no full config snapshots.

Rafael Mendes (requested changes): Add request_id and deployment/route identifiers consistently; we’ll need this during incident-style triage when customers report timeouts after tier switches.

Ethan Park: Added request_id to formatter; standardized target_resource_id mapping for deployment config vs route config updates. Added integration assertion for request_id presence.

Benji Okafor (nit): Can we standardize naming as cost_efficient everywhere? Also prefer actor_type service vs user.

Ethan Park: Updated subtype emitter to normalize cost_efficient; added actor_type enum mapping consistent with existing audit events.

Chloe Martin (comment): Console needs to show who changed it; is actor_email available in the audit viewer API?

Ethan Park: Yes for user actors; not for service principals. No API changes needed; viewer already supports displaying actor_email if present.

CI: - build: pass - unit: pass - lint: pass - integration: pass

Outcome: Merged (squash) into main. Follow-up suggested in Linear: add targeted audit subtypes for high-risk batching knobs and include “effective config explain” linkage (see PR #18470) in audit viewer for one-click debugging.
